articles.title: Visa delays and policy uncertainty projected to reduce foreign enrolment in the US by more than 100,000 students this fall
articles.summary: A new analysis by NAFSA and JB International projects that visa processing delays and upcoming policy changes will reduce international student enrolment in the United States by more than 100,000 students this fall. The projection is based on institutional responses collected in IIE’s Spring 2026 Snapshot on International Educational Exchange.
articles.insight:
This news signals potential softening in US-bound demand amid growing visa processing bottlenecks and policy ambiguity, though it remains unclear how much reflects temporary administrative delays versus longer-term shifts in student preferences across key source markets.  
Admissions teams should monitor real-time application trends from top sending countries, track competitor messaging around visa support and processing timelines, and assess whether their own pre-enrolment services—especially visa guidance—need refinement to address rising applicant anxiety.

articles.title: Report: US considering a $100,000 fee for Optional Practical Training
articles.summary: The Trump administration is reportedly considering imposing a $100,000 fee on international students seeking Optional Practical Training (OPT) in the United States after graduating from American universities. This potential policy change was disclosed by The Wall Street Journal, citing sources familiar with the matter.
articles.insight:
This proposed $100,000 OPT fee—though unconfirmed and potentially subject to legal or political hurdles—could dampen US appeal for international students weighing post-study work value, especially from price-sensitive markets like India and Nigeria, thereby indirectly reshaping regional demand patterns across English-speaking study destinations.  
Admissions teams should track official USCIS and DHS announcements closely, benchmark competitor messaging on post-study work pathways, and assess whether their institution’s career support services need enhanced emphasis in marketing to offset perceived US visa uncertainty.

articles.title: U.K. government pauses Chevening Fellowships for a year over likely budget cuts
articles.summary: The U.K. government has paused Chevening Fellowships for one year due to anticipated budget cuts. This suspension affects specific fellowship programmes—including the CRISP programme for science and innovation, the cybersecurity fellowship, and the South Asia Journalism Programme—while Chevening Scholarships remain open for applications.
articles.insight:
The pause in Chevening Fellowships—particularly those targeting South Asian professionals in science, cybersecurity, and journalism—may modestly increase demand for alternative postgraduate pathways in the UK and competing destinations, though broader student recruitment trends remain influenced more by visa policy, cost-of-living, and labour market outcomes than this targeted suspension.  
Admissions teams should monitor application volumes from South Asia for taught master’s and professional programmes, especially in STEM and media, while tracking whether UK Home Office announcements on post-study work or skilled worker visas follow this fiscal tightening, as those signals will carry greater weight for prospective students.

articles.title: Thailand steps up crackdown on foreigners engaged in illegal business activities
articles.summary: Thailand has intensified enforcement actions against illegal business networks and suspected nominee shareholding. Joint inspections were conducted in hotels and establishments in Bangkok’s Huai Khwang District, as reported by the Government Public Relations Department.
articles.insight:
This news reflects Thailand’s broader regulatory tightening on foreign economic activity, which may indirectly influence regional student mobility patterns if perceived as signalling stricter immigration or residency enforcement—though direct impacts on enrolment demand remain uncertain without evidence of spillover effects on student visas.  
Admissions teams should monitor Thai government announcements on visa policy updates and track whether regional sentiment shifts among Southeast Asian students, particularly regarding perceptions of Thailand as a study destination or transit hub, while continuing to prioritise established recruitment channels.
